chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from Abi al-Mi'za, from Abi Hamzah al-Thumali, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever frequently recites Surah Qaaf in his obligatory and supererogatory prayers, Allah will expand his livelihood, give him his Book in his right hand, and call him to an easy accounting.
ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for frequently reciting Surah Qaaf in prayers?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), linking the habitual recitation of Surah Qaaf in obligatory and voluntary prayers to tangible spiritual benefits. The promise of 'sustenance' (rizq) and a 'right-hand book' signifies both material provision and high status in the Hereafter, while the 'light reckoning' reflects the purifying effect of consistent dhikr on one's sins.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan from Abi al-Mi’za from Abi Hamzah al-Thumali from Abi Ja’far (a.s.) who said:

Whoever has been reciting Surah Qaaf in his obligatory and supererogatory prayers Allah would grant addition and increase in his livelihood, his record of Deeds would be in his right hand and (on the Day of Judgment) his accounting would be in an easy and peaceful way.
